body_text:
Every propositional formula is logically equivalent to one in
*Disjunctive Normal Form* (DNF) and to one in *Conjunctive Normal
Form* (CNF).

A formula in DNF is a disjunction of conjunctions of literals
(variables or their negations), analogous to a sum-of-products in
elementary algebra. It can be constructed directly from the
formula's truth table by taking a conjunction for each row where
the formula evaluates to true, and forming the disjunction of
these conjunctions.

Dually, a formula in CNF is a conjunction of disjunctions of
literals (a product-of-sums). Although the transformation into
either normal form can produce an exponential increase in formula
length, the normal forms guarantee that every Boolean truth
function admits a completely explicit, canonical representation.
